brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether a blood pressure treatment strategy during pregnancy to achieve targets that are recommended for non-pregnant reproductive-age adults (\<140/90 mmHg) compared ACOG- recommended standard during pregnancy (no treatment unless BP is severe) is effective and safe.

eligibility_table.criterion: Women with chronic hypertension in pregnancy with new or untreated chronic hypertension, blood pressure 140-159 systolic or 90-104 diastolic OR known chronic hypertension on monotherapy and taking any antihypertensive and blood pressure ≤159/104 (including those with blood pressure <140/90);
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage, but there is no information on chronic hypertension or blood pressure readings.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's current blood pressure between 140-159 systolic or 90-104 diastolic?

eligibility_table.criterion: *If a dipstick value at screening is more than trace, a clean catch or catheter urine should be obtained and re-tested by dipstick. If this shows trace or absence of protein, the patient is included. If it again shows 1+ protein, the patient is excluded until a 24-hr urine <300mg/24hr or p/c ratio is <0.3. If a p/c ratio is >0.3, the patient may be included if a 24-hour urine is < 300 mg.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information on proteinuria or creatinine levels to evaluate eligibility.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's protein-to-creatinine (p/c) ratio ≤0.3 based on a 24-hour urine collection?
